newsitem.title: FRANCE: Publicis sister threatens to sue Somarel.
newsitem.headline: Publicis sister threatens to sue Somarel.

text.p: Michele Bleustein-Blanchet, daughter of deceased Publicis founder Marcel Bleustein-Blanchet, said in an interview published on Monday she could sue Publicis holding firm Somarel if talks with her sister, Elisabeth Badinter, did not succeed.
Bleustein-Blanchet told financial daily Les Echos that Badinter was accorded a blocking minority in Somarel in 1987. She discovered this when her father died in April 1996.
"There is a real disagreement over the capital situation. I am seeking a change in statute and the conversion of Somarel shares into Publicis SA shares," she said.
She said she consulted several legal experts and was told she had good reasons to obtain the disappearance of Somarel.
She told Les Echos that she had asked SBC Warburg to value her direct and indirect holdings in Publicis and to seek a buyer by August.
"I have given the bank SBC Warburg instructions to evaluate my share and to look for investors between now and the month of August," she said.

"There are talks with Elisabeth Badinter which are not going very well...Either these talks conclude quickly, or I take legal action against the company Somarel, which I consider to be fraudulous," she said.
Since her father's death just over a year ago, Bleustein-Blanchet has owned about 20 percent of Publicis directly and indirectly.
She has a direct stake of 7.6 percent in the French advertising group, and a third of Somarel, which owns 38.4 percent of Publicis' capital and 45 percent of its voting rights.
Asked if she would sell her 7.6-percent direct holding in Publicis on the market initially, Bleustein-Blanchet said she preferred to sell her holding as a block.

"I find it is a particularly opportune moment when (Publicis chairman) Maurice Levy has a strategy of internationalising the group. That said, I do not exclude selling part of it (the holding)," she said.
She added that she had no disagreement with Levy's strategy for Publicis.
